_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: The token from api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token is short lived and must be exchanged straight away. Store only the long-lived one.

A long-lived token lasts 60 days and is refreshed for another 60 by calling refresh_access_token with it. A connector left idle for two months is dead and has to be reconnected by hand - refresh on a schedule, not on first failure.

This is Instagram API with Instagram Login, the setup that does NOT require a Facebook Page to be linked. That is the reason it is chosen over the Facebook-Login variant, which routes through graph.facebook.com and needs a linked Page.

The scope names above are the current ones. business_basic, business_content_publish, business_manage_comments and business_manage_messages are the old spellings and were deprecated on 27 January 2025; anything still sending them fails.
Requires an Instagram professional account - Business or Creator. Consumer accounts cannot be reached by any Instagram API, which is what the connector's badge means.

Needs a Meta app the user owns. Standard Access covers professional accounts the user themselves owns or manages and has added in the App Dashboard; reaching anyone else's account needs App Review. Flux is the former case.
The token exchange takes a client secret, which a desktop binary cannot keep. The user supplies their own Meta app's ID and secret, as with the Facebook connector - Flux ships no shared credential.
graph.instagram.com is the host for Instagram Login. graph.facebook.com is the host for the Facebook-Login variant, and the two are not interchangeable - a token from one is rejected by the other.
All edges paginate by cursor. Ordering is not supported, and only the User Insights edge supports time-based pagination.
Hashtag search and the Page node exist only under the Facebook-Login variant, so no hashtag operation is offered here.

create_media_container.label: Stage a post
create_media_container.notes: Two-step publish: this returns a container id, which is then passed to media_publish. The media has to be reachable at a public URL - Instagram fetches it, Flux does not upload bytes.

publish_media.label: Publish a post
publish_media.notes: Stories are Business-only; every other media type works for Creator accounts too.

rate_limits.note: Meta throttles rather than bans; a 429 means back off. Content publishing has its own published daily cap on top of the general limit - read it before wiring a posting workflow to more than a handful of posts a day.

notes: The capability list, the two host URLs, the scope rename and its January 2025 deprecation, the professional-account restriction and the pagination and ordering limits are taken verbatim from the Meta pages the user supplied.

The four OAuth URLs and the 60-day long-lived token lifetime come from Meta's own oauth-authorize, oauth-access-token and business-login reference pages via search, not from the supplied text - developers.facebook.com is not reachable from the Flux container. Verified as `search` rather than `vendor-docs` for that reason; re-check them against the reference before the first live connect.

Operation paths follow the /me and /{node-id}/{edge} shape the reference documents. The node and edge names are from Meta's reference; the exact field lists are not, and a first call should ask for a minimal fields set and widen from what comes back.
